papers.t: Eltrombopag during induction chemotherapy in older patients with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia is safe and reduces platelet transfusion requirements: The EPAG-2015 French Innovative Leukemia Organization phase 2 randomized trial
papers.c: This study failed to demonstrate a survival advantage after eltrombopag addition, at variance with previous reports, but shows that initiating eltrombopag after chemotherapy washout is feasible and safe, and resulted in a decreased need for platelet transfusions.
ab: Background

Elderly patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) treated with intensive chemotherapy are at risk of developing thrombopenia, which requires platelet transfusions. It would be interesting to provide them with thrombopoietin receptor agonists such as eltrombopag.
Methods

The EPAG-2015 multicenter phase 2 trial (18 French hospitals from October 2018 to June 2021) blindly randomized elderly patients (aged ≥60 years) with placebo or eltrombopag administered on Day 11 after induction chemotherapy and continued until AML response evaluation (Day 45) or a platelet count of >100 × 109/L. A cohort of 110 patients with a median age of 70 years was included and randomized (55 per arm) to receive placebo or eltrombopag.
Results

After induction, 90 patients (81.8%) achieved complete response (CR) or CR with incomplete reconstitution (CRi) (45 in each group), including 74 patients with CR (38 with eltrombopag and 36 with placebo). With a median follow-up for alive patients of 20.9 months the primary objective was not reached, given that there was no difference in overall survival (hazard ratio, 1.59; 95% CI, 0.65-3.89; p = .31). Eltrombopag, however, did not lead to increased grade 3/4 adverse events, and was associated with a lower median number of platelet transfusions (eight; interquartile range [IQR], 6-14; vs. 10; IQR, 7-14; i.e., a 20% benefit).
Conclusions

This study failed to demonstrate a survival advantage after eltrombopag addition, at variance with previous reports, but shows that initiating eltrombopag after chemotherapy washout is feasible and safe, and resulted in a decreased need for platelet transfusions.

papers.t: Prognostic Impact of FLT3-ITD Microclones in AML: An EHA AML-Specialized Working Group Study
papers.c: At relapse, 15 of 33 (45%) evaluable patients remained FLT3-ITD+, with 10 expanding the original microclone. In conclusion, FLT3-ITDm are associated with older age, secondary AML, and with expansion of the FLT3-ITD clone upon relapse, thereby providing a rationale for the evaluation of FLT3i in randomized clinical trials.
ab: The 2022 ELN recommendations reclassified fms-like tyrosine kinase-3 (FLT3)-ITD mutated acute myeloid leukemia (AML) as intermediate-risk, irrespective of allelic ratio (AR), and designated capillary electrophoresis (CE) as the preferred detection method. However, CE requires substantial expertise, particularly to identify FLT3-ITD microclones (FLT3-ITDm; AR < 0.05), whose clinical significance remains uncertain. Herein, we investigated diagnostic aspects and the prognostic impact of FLT3-ITDm. An initial methodological study performed on 48 FLT3-ITD+ samples, with AR 0.001-6.00, showed overall concordance between CE and next-generation sequencing (NGS) results (p < 0.001), with only three microclones (AR: 0.002, 0.001, and 0.008) identified by CE and not by NGS. We next analyzed 658 AML patients diagnosed with a FLT3-ITD+ AML (n = 446 with AR ≥ 0.05, and n = 212 with a microclone) between 2017 and 2022. Patients with FLT3-ITDm, as compared to patients with AR ≥ 0.05, were older, more often had secondary-type AML, and displayed a higher prevalence of myelodysplasia-related gene mutations, while NPM1-mutation frequency was similar in the two groups. Complete remission rates were lower in FLT3-ITDm (74%) than in patients with AR ≥ 0.05 (88%) treated with intensive chemotherapy without FLT3-inhibitors (FLT3i). In the intensively treated subgroup, multivariate analyses demonstrated that age, NPM1 mutation, and allogeneic stem cell transplantation, rather than FLT3-ITD AR, were independent predictors of disease-free survival. At relapse, 15 of 33 (45%) evaluable patients remained FLT3-ITD+, with 10 expanding the original microclone. In conclusion, FLT3-ITDm are associated with older age, secondary AML, and with expansion of the FLT3-ITD clone upon relapse, thereby providing a rationale for the evaluation of FLT3i in randomized clinical trials.

papers.t: STAG2 mutation predicts superior posttransplant survival in acute myeloid leukemia treated with low-intensity induction
Immune landscape and immunotherapeutic strategies for the treatment of TP53-mutated acute myeloid leukemia
papers.c: While TP53-specific clinical data are currently available for only a limited number of immunotherapeutic approaches, several emerging modalities have demonstrated biological or clinical activity in AML more broadly and possess a strong biological rationale for investigation in TP53-mutated disease based on the unique immune landscape of this molecular subtype. This review summarizes the immune mechanisms of treatment resistance in TP53-mutated AML, provides an overview of the current landscape of immunotherapy, and discusses future directions, including rational combination strategies, patient selection, and optimized therapeutic timing to achieve durable responses and improve survival in this high-risk population.
ab: TP53-mutated acute myeloid leukemia (AML) represents the treatment-refractory subtype of AML, characterized by high relapse rates and poor clinical outcomes. Despite advancements in AML treatment with currently approved agents and allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation, overall survival for patients with TP53-mutated AML remains dismal, underscoring the urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies. TP53 mutations contribute to treatment resistance by impairing apoptosis and fostering immune evasion through mechanisms such as regulatory immune cell expansion, immune checkpoint overexpression, and dysregulation of the bone marrow microenvironment. Immunotherapy has emerged as an area of active investigation to overcome therapeutic resistance and improve clinical outcomes. While TP53-specific clinical data are currently available for only a limited number of immunotherapeutic approaches, several emerging modalities have demonstrated biological or clinical activity in AML more broadly and possess a strong biological rationale for investigation in TP53-mutated disease based on the unique immune landscape of this molecular subtype. This review summarizes the immune mechanisms of treatment resistance in TP53-mutated AML, provides an overview of the current landscape of immunotherapy, and discusses future directions, including rational combination strategies, patient selection, and optimized therapeutic timing to achieve durable responses and improve survival in this high-risk population.

papers.t: Prolonged treatment-free remission after venetoclax in combination with a hypomethylating agent in acute myeloid leukemia with inv(16)
papers.c: This case provides proof-of-concept that carefully selected CBF-AML patients achieving sustained MRD-negative remission with HMA/ven can successfully discontinue therapy. Prospective evaluation of HMA/ven in unfit CBF-AML patients, weighed against dose-attenuated intensive chemotherapy, is needed to define its role and optimal duration.
ab: Core binding factor acute myeloid leukemia (CBF-AML)-defined by t(8;21) or inv(16) chromosomal rearrangements-is classified as favorable-risk disease per the European LeukemiaNet 2022 risk model and is typically treated with intensive chemotherapy. Patients unsuitable for intensive therapy increasingly receive hypomethylating agents plus venetoclax (HMA/ven), though CBF-AML was excluded from pivotal trials of this regimen. Furthermore, HMA/ven is typically administered as indefinite therapy in AML; however, there is increasing interest in exploring the feasibility of therapy cessation given persistent treatment-free remissions with this regimen. Here, we report the first case of sustained treatment-free remission following HMA/ven in CBF-AML. Features in this case that suggest a higher likelihood of achieving a durable treatment-free remission include inv(16) disease and rapid measurable residual disease (MRD) clearance. We summarize the current retrospective data comparing response rates of inv(16) vs. t(8;21) AML to HMA/ven: inv(16) AML consistently exhibits higher response rates compared with t(8;21) disease, although an overall survival benefit is not well established. Emerging data also suggest achieving MRD-negative complete remission after induction may predict more durable outcomes. This case provides proof-of-concept that carefully selected CBF-AML patients achieving sustained MRD-negative remission with HMA/ven can successfully discontinue therapy. Prospective evaluation of HMA/ven in unfit CBF-AML patients, weighed against dose-attenuated intensive chemotherapy, is needed to define its role and optimal duration.

Therapeutic Synergy and Immune Activation by SUMOylation Pathway Inhibition in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
papers.c: In immunocompetent models, TAK-981 induced systemic immune remodeling, including increased CD8⁺ T-cell and NK-cell frequencies, memory T-cell polarization, and sustained elevation of granzyme B, IFN-γ, and TNF-α. These findings support SUMO pathway inhibition with TAK-981 as a promising combinatorial strategy to improve treatment durability and overcome resistance in AML through both direct anti-leukemic effects and immune reprogramming.
ab: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a clinically aggressive malignancy with poor outcomes driven by frequent relapse and therapeutic resistance. Because the SUMOylation pathway regulates genome maintenance, transcription control, and immune evasion, it represents a promising therapeutic target in AML. We evaluated the therapeutic and immunomodulatory effects of TAK-981 using patient-derived AML samples and preclinical models. Expression of SUMO pathway components (SAE1, SAE2, and UBC9) was assessed in newly diagnosed AML and correlated with bone marrow blast burden. Anti-leukemic activity and drug interactions with venetoclax and gilteritinib were tested in vitro and ex vivo and validated in xenograft models, while immune reprogramming was characterized in immunocompetent AML models by profiling immune subsets and effector cytokine/mediator signatures. SAE1, SAE2, and UBC9 were significantly higher in bulk diagnostic specimens than in remission specimens and positively correlated with blast percentages. TAK-981 showed potent anti-leukemic activity and synergized with venetoclax and gilteritinib in vitro and ex vivo. In xenograft studies, TAK-981 enhanced the efficacy of both agents, and a four-week triplet regimen produced durable disease control and superior survival benefit with a favorable safety profile. In immunocompetent models, TAK-981 induced systemic immune remodeling, including increased CD8⁺ T-cell and NK-cell frequencies, memory T-cell polarization, and sustained elevation of granzyme B, IFN-γ, and TNF-α. These findings support SUMO pathway inhibition with TAK-981 as a promising combinatorial strategy to improve treatment durability and overcome resistance in AML through both direct anti-leukemic effects and immune reprogramming.

papers.t: Acute promyelocytic leukemia with clonal hematopoiesis: a case study of APL in complete molecular remission transitioning to MDS/MPN and its clinical implications
Single-Cell RNA sequencing analysis of cellular heterogeneity and microenvironment-driven signaling networks in acute myeloid leukemia
papers.c: Gene-set analysis showed consistent interferon-gamma responses across key cell populations. These findings provide a transcriptome-based, hypothesis-generating framework linking cellular heterogeneity, microenvironmental signaling, and therapeutic vulnerabilities in adverse-risk AML.
ab: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) exhibits cellular heterogeneity that complicates tumor micro-environment (TME) characterization. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with BayesPrism bulk transcriptomic deconvolution to compare cellular composition by cytogenetic risk (favorable versus adverse). scRNA-seq identified immune and malignant hematopoietic populations, including leukemia stem cell (LSC) and granulocyte-monocyte-progenitor clusters, with recurrent alterations involving chromosomes 5, 7, and 8. TCGA-LAML deconvolution reconstructed cell-type-resolved profiles and linked adverse-risk AML to poorer overall survival. CellChat showed expanded cell-cell communication in adverse-risk disease involving SPP1, CXCL, GRN, TENASCIN, VCAM, and WNT signaling, particularly in leukemic stem-like and megakaryocytic compartments. Pathway analysis implicated differentiation arrest and immune exhaustion. In-silico repurposing nominated belinostat: ASGARD ranked it the top HDAC inhibitor, and scRANK characterized its HDAC1-centered target network. Gene-set analysis showed consistent interferon-gamma responses across key cell populations. These findings provide a transcriptome-based, hypothesis-generating framework linking cellular heterogeneity, microenvironmental signaling, and therapeutic vulnerabilities in adverse-risk AML.

papers.t: Rapid proteasomal degradation of mutant feline McDonough sarcoma-like tyrosine kinase-3 overcomes inhibitor resistance mechanisms of acute myeloid leukemia cells
papers.c: Accordingly, leukemia cells with acquired resistance to MA191 lack such mutations. We offer a framework for fast-acting next-generation FLT3 degraders that overcome resistance mechanisms to classical inhibitors.
ab: The hyperactive kinase FLT3-ITD causes acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and is a prognostic biomarker. We synthesized and characterized MA191 as a novel von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) E3 ubiquitin ligase-based proteolysis targeting chimera (PROTAC) for FLT3. MA191 induces apoptosis in cultured and primary AML patient cells harboring FLT3-ITD (IC50=9.6-11 nM; EC50=0.001-0.883 µM). Comparison with a VHL-binding-deficient stereoisomer of MA191 demonstrates that FLT3-ITD degradation is superior to kinase inhibition (p < 0.03). Rapid depletion of FLT3-ITD by MA191 (DC50=10 nM) requires VHL, neddylation, proteasome activity, and the pro-apoptotic BH3-only protein BIM. MA191 reduces FLT3-ITD prior to apoptosis, uncovering apoptosis-independent roles of BIM for protein stability. Higher expression levels of FLT3 in leukemia cells than in healthy cells (n = 3675/n = 1249) are associated with worse AML patient survival (p = 0.0099). MA191 does not harm healthy blood and bone marrow progenitor cells or myeloid cell differentiation. In Danio rerio larvae, MA191 halts AML cell proliferation without significant toxicity. Human stromal cell interactions and mutations in the tyrosine kinase domain of FLT3-ITD that confer resistance to FLT3 inhibitors do not abolish anti-leukemic effects of MA191. Accordingly, leukemia cells with acquired resistance to MA191 lack such mutations. We offer a framework for fast-acting next-generation FLT3 degraders that overcome resistance mechanisms to classical inhibitors.

papers.t: Characterization of chemoresistant cell populations improves risk stratification and therapy prediction in pediatric acute myeloid leukemia
papers.c: This approach identifies a patient subgroup comprising 20% of the patients who do not undergo SCT, with a 5-year event-free survival below 40%, and accounting for nearly half of all deaths in this population. Molecular characterization of these cell populations reveals therapeutic vulnerabilities and potential targeted treatment strategies for high-risk pAML, providing a framework for precision oncology diagnosis and intervention.
ab: Most pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (pAML) patients achieve complete remission after chemotherapy, yet nearly 40% ultimately relapse and die from their disease. High risk cases are typically referred for stem cell transplantation (SCT) in first remission, but because SCT is associated with substantial toxicity and cures after relapse are rare, accurate risk prediction is critical. Here, we show that combining the detection of chemoresistant cell populations, inferred from single-cell transcriptomic profiles of paired diagnosis-relapse samples, and cytogenetic biomarkers at diagnosis with measurable residual disease after induction chemotherapy, substantially improves risk prediction. This approach identifies a patient subgroup comprising 20% of the patients who do not undergo SCT, with a 5-year event-free survival below 40%, and accounting for nearly half of all deaths in this population. Molecular characterization of these cell populations reveals therapeutic vulnerabilities and potential targeted treatment strategies for high-risk pAML, providing a framework for precision oncology diagnosis and intervention.

papers.t: Quizartinib in older patients (aged ≥60 years) with newly diagnosed FLT3-ITDpositive acute myeloid leukemia: subgroup analyses from QuANTUM-First
papers.c: Higher frequency of gastrointestinal treatmentemergent adverse events and a longer time to hematologic recovery were observed with quizartinib. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02668653.
ab: The QuANTUM-First trial (NCT02668653) showed quizartinib significantly improved overall survival (OS) versus placebo when added to standard chemotherapy and as maintenance monotherapy in patients with newly diagnosed, FMS-related tyrosine kinase 3-internal tandem duplication (FLT3-ITD)-positive acute myeloid leukemia. These post hoc analyses further evaluated clinical outcomes in older patients (≥60 years). Median OS was 17.5 and 14.2 months with quizartinib (n=107) and placebo (n=109), respectively (hazard ratio [HR], 0.91; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.66-1.26). Complete remission rates were similar (quizartinib, 53%; placebo, 55%), but median duration of complete response was numerically longer with quizartinib (15.9 vs. 9.0 months; HR, 0.92; 95% CI: 0.59-1.42). Cumulative incidence of relapse at 24 months was lower (quizartinib, 44%; placebo, 51%) and relapse-free survival was numerically longer (median, 16.6 vs. 9.7 months; HR, 0.91; 95% CI: 0.59-1.42) with quizartinib. NPM1 (quizartinib 62%, placebo 61%) and DNMT3A (51% and 50%) mutations were common and often co-mutated together (NPM1+DNMT3A; 38% and 38%), with each mutation or combination associated with numerically longer median OS with quizartinib (vs. placebo): 25.8 versus 15.4 (NPM1), 15.6 versus 11.5 (DNMT3A), and 21.8 versus 9.7 months (NPM1+DNMT3A), respectively. Quizartinib showed manageable tolerability for older patients, with safety generally similar to the placebo arm. Higher frequency of gastrointestinal treatmentemergent adverse events and a longer time to hematologic recovery were observed with quizartinib. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02668653.

papers.t: Patients' preferences for accepting risks and uncertainty in AML treatments within European public health care systems: a cross-sectional study in Finland, Italy, and Germany
papers.c: Preference heterogeneity was identified. Complete remission was ranked most important followed by scientific evidence and risk of long-term side effects.
ab: The aim of this study was to identify what tradeoffs patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) are willing to make between different treatment attributes when choosing between chemotherapy and novel targeted therapies involving higher uncertainty, within the context of European publicly funded health‑care systems. A survey with a probabilistic threshold technique and a ranking exercise were distributed to patients with AML in Finland, Germany, and Italy. Respondents (n = 68) were presented with two treatment options described by six attributes. Interval regressions were used to analyze the threshold intervals for each attribute. Mean threshold values for accepting targeted treatment were 82% chance of complete remission, 48% risk of short-term side effects, 10% for long-term side effects, and two weeks for treatment time in hospital. Preference heterogeneity was identified. Complete remission was ranked most important followed by scientific evidence and risk of long-term side effects.

papers.t: Time burden and treatment patterns of patients with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia receiving parenteral hypomethylating agents in combination with venetoclax
papers.c: Median time to discontinuation or death on HMA therapy when considering any HMA cycle and label-conforming cycles (≥16 days of venetoclax supply; ≥4/3 days of azacitidine/decitabine) was 5.2 and 2.8 months, respectively. These findings highlight the substantial time burden associated with HMA combined with venetoclax.
ab: Parenteral hypomethylating agents (HMAs) combined with venetoclax are a first-line treatment for newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) considered ineligible for intensive chemotherapy. Using a retrospective claims database (Humana Healthcare Research Database; 01/01/2019-12/31/2024), time burden, time at home, treatment patterns and persistence were characterized among adults with newly diagnosed AML treated with HMA + venetoclax, from index (first parenteral HMA claim) through end of follow-up (earliest of death, end of insurance eligibility, or end of data). Patients (n = 737; median follow-up: 8.0 months) spent a mean of 11.9 days per month on healthcare visits, with 65.0% of time spent at home or not receiving cancer care. Median time to discontinuation or death on HMA therapy when considering any HMA cycle and label-conforming cycles (≥16 days of venetoclax supply; ≥4/3 days of azacitidine/decitabine) was 5.2 and 2.8 months, respectively. These findings highlight the substantial time burden associated with HMA combined with venetoclax.

papers.t: IDH2 p.R172 mutation Predicts Superior Outcomes in IDH-mutated Acute Myeloid Leukemia or Myelodysplastic Syndrome patients undergoing Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation: a retrospective study from the Grupo Español de Trasplante Hematopoyético y Terapia Celular (GETH-TC)
papers.c: Collectively, our findings suggest that AML/MDS patients harboring IDH2 p.R172 mutations may experience particularly favorable outcomes after allo-HCT. Whether this advantage reflects an intrinsically favorable disease biology or increased sensitivity to graft-versus-leukemia effects remains unclear and warrants confirmation in larger, prospective studies.
ab: Background

The prognostic impact of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutations (IDH1 and IDH2) in adult patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) remains unclear.
Objectives
To determine whether specific IDH mutations (IDH1, IDH2 p.R140, IDH2 p.R172) are associated with differences in survival and relapse risk after allo-HCT in AML and MDS.
Study Design

We conducted a retrospective multicenter study including patients with IDH-mutated AML or MDS who underwent their first allo-HCT within the Spanish Group for Hematopoietic Transplantation and Cellular Therapy (GETH-TC) network. Patients were stratified according to IDH subtype (IDH1, IDH2 p.R140, and IDH2 p.R172). Inclusion criteria comprised a confirmed diagnosis of AML or MDS, the presence of an IDH1 or IDH2 mutation, and receipt of a first allo-HCT. The primary endpoint was the 1-year overall survival (OS).
Results

A total of 101 patients were included from 9 EBMT/GETH-TC institutions. Among them, 46 (46%) harbored IDH1 p.R132 mutations, while 55 (54%) had IDH2 mutations. Within the IDH2-mutated group, 29 (53%) had IDH2 p.R140, 15 (27%) had IDH2 p.R172, and 11 (20%) had an unspecified IDH2 mutation subtype. The median follow-up time was 21.2 months (IQR, 17.5-30.6). At 1-year, overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), relapse incidence (RI), and non-relapse mortality (NRM) were 79% (95% CI, 71.2-88.5), 75% (95% CI, 66.6-85.0), 16% (95% CI, 7.6-24.2), and 9.5% (95% CI, 3.1-14.7), respectively. IDH2 p.R172 mutated patients showed significantly improved outcomes, with 1-year OS of 93% compared with 74% in the remaining patients (p=0.05). Notably, no relapses were observed in the IDH2 p.R172 group during the follow-up period (p<0.001). In multivariate analysis, the IDH2 p.R172 mutation was independently associated with absence of relapse (p<0.001) during follow-up, prolonged PFS (HR 0.10; 95% CI, 0.01-0.90; p=0.04), and improved OS (HR 0.09; 95% CI, 0.01-0.80; p=0.03).
Conclusion

Collectively, our findings suggest that AML/MDS patients harboring IDH2 p.R172 mutations may experience particularly favorable outcomes after allo-HCT. Whether this advantage reflects an intrinsically favorable disease biology or increased sensitivity to graft-versus-leukemia effects remains unclear and warrants confirmation in larger, prospective studies.

Prognostic Impact of FLT3-ITD Allelic Ratio in AML Patients Treated With High-Dose Anthracycline and a FLT3 Inhibitor
papers.c: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation was associated with improved relapse-free (aHR 0.40, 95% CI 0.29-0.55, p < 0.001) and event-free survival (aHR 0.37, 95% CI 0.27-0.51, p < 0.001), but not OS. These results indicate that FLT3-ITD AR has no independent prognostic impact in younger AML patients treated with intensive anthracycline-based chemotherapy and midostaurin in contemporary clinical practice.
ab: The prognostic value of FLT3 internal tandem duplication (FLT3-ITD) in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) has traditionally been stratified according to the ITD/wild-type allelic ratio (AR) and NPM1 co-mutation status. We evaluated the prognostic impact of FLT3-ITD AR in 459 newly diagnosed AML patients younger than 60 years enrolled in the prospective BIG-1 study, all treated with high-dose anthracycline-based induction. From 2018 onward, midostaurin was added for FLT3-mutated cases. AR was not associated with composite complete remission (81.7% vs. 79.6% in low vs. high AR, p = 0.85), overall survival (OS) (median 7.6 vs. 6.9 years, p = 0.25), relapse-free survival (median 2.0 vs. 1.7 years, p = 0.50), or event-free survival (median 1.4 vs. 1.2 years, p = 0.58). In multivariable analyses, only midostaurin exposure (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.69, 95% CI 0.50-0.95, p = 0.024) and adverse ELN-2022 risk (aHR 1.66, 95% CI 1.18-2.34, p = 0.004) were independently associated with OS. Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation was associated with improved relapse-free (aHR 0.40, 95% CI 0.29-0.55, p < 0.001) and event-free survival (aHR 0.37, 95% CI 0.27-0.51, p < 0.001), but not OS. These results indicate that FLT3-ITD AR has no independent prognostic impact in younger AML patients treated with intensive anthracycline-based chemotherapy and midostaurin in contemporary clinical practice.

papers.t: Secondary minimally differentiated acute leukemia with plasmacytoid dendritic cell differentiation (pDC-AML) following chemoradiotherapy for Ewing sarcoma in a child: biallelic EZH2 inactivation
papers.c: Genetic analysis revealed a complex karyotype with del(7q), biallelic EZH2 inactivation, 3q duplication involving MECOM, and PTPN11 mutation. This pediatric therapy-related case with a distinct genetic profile expands the spectrum of pDC-AML and highlights the diagnostic pitfall of CD123+/CD4+ immunophenotype in myeloid neoplasms with pDC differentiation.
ab: The diagnosis of myeloid neoplasms with plasmacytoid dendritic cell (pDC) differentiation is challenging due to immunophenotypic overlap with BPDCN. We describe an 8-year-old boy with a history of Ewing sarcoma treated with chemotherapy and radiotherapy who developed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) two years later. Bone marrow met criteria for AML with minimal differentiation: blasts expressed CD34, CD117, CD33, and CD7 but lacked myeloperoxidase; scattered TCF4+ cells indicated a minor pDC component. Concurrently, 23.6% of pleural fluid cells exhibited a classic pDC immunophenotype (CD123+bright, CD304+, CD4+, HLA-DR+bright, CD56-, TCF4+ by immunohistochemistry). Genetic analysis revealed a complex karyotype with del(7q), biallelic EZH2 inactivation, 3q duplication involving MECOM, and PTPN11 mutation. This pediatric therapy-related case with a distinct genetic profile expands the spectrum of pDC-AML and highlights the diagnostic pitfall of CD123+/CD4+ immunophenotype in myeloid neoplasms with pDC differentiation.

papers.t: The speed of sequencing: Rapid molecular testing in acute myeloid leukaemia
papers.c: Commentary on: Helena Castellet, Rapid molecular screening of adult AML: Experience from the Spanish Grupo Cooperativo de Estudio y Tratamiento de las Leucemias Agudas y Mielodisplásicas (CETLAM) cooperative group. Br J Haematol 2026 (Online ahead of print). doi: 10.1111/bjh.70865.
ab: Rapid molecular testing has become increasingly important in acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), where timely identification of disease defining, prognostic and actionable genetic abnormalities directly influence early clinical management. Castellet et al. demonstrate that a centralized rapid molecular screening programme for newly diagnosed AML patients has benefit in reliably identifying favourable-risk patients and potentially actionable therapeutic targets. They show that rapid molecular testing is complementary, although it should not replace comprehensive next-generation sequencing (NGS) and cytogenetic analysis-balancing curation of important genes and sequencing strategies. papers.t: Sequential emergence of FLT3-ITD and BCR::ABL1 during disease progression in relapsed acute myeloid leukemia
papers.c: Despite no ABL1 kinase domain mutations, imatinib and ponatinib failed to control the disease. These findings suggest that BCR::ABL1 emergence may represent a bypass resistance mechanism arising under quizartinib-associated selective pressure.
ab: Emergence of BCR::ABL1 during FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3) inhibitor therapy is a rare resistance mechanism in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). We report a case of relapsed AML with sequential clonal evolution after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT). A previously healthy man in his 30s was diagnosed with AML with maturation; initial cytogenetics were normal, and both FLT3-internal tandem duplication (FLT3-ITD) and BCR::ABL1 were absent, while targeted sequencing identified an FBXW7 mutation. After induction failure, he underwent allo-HSCT. At post-transplant relapse during venetoclax plus azacitidine maintenance, FLT3-ITD and WT1 mutations newly emerged. Quizartinib induced remission, but a second relapse occurred with emergence of BCR::ABL1 while FLT3-ITD persisted. Cytogenetics showed t(9;22)(q34;q11), and FISH confirmed BCR::ABL1 fusion in 73% of bone marrow cells, with the minor transcript (p190) confirmed by quantitative PCR. Despite no ABL1 kinase domain mutations, imatinib and ponatinib failed to control the disease. These findings suggest that BCR::ABL1 emergence may represent a bypass resistance mechanism arising under quizartinib-associated selective pressure.

papers.t: Hu B, Reagan PM, Sehn LH, et al. Subgroup analysis of older patients ≥60 years with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in the phase 3 POLARIX study. Blood Adv. 2025;9(10):2489-2499

Zamtocabtagene autoleucel, a tandem CD20-CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy, for second line treatment of large B-cell lymphoma in patients ineligible for transplantation (DALY 2-EU): primary analysis of an open-label, multicentre, randomised phase 2 study
papers.c: The risk-benefit ratio observed in the DALY 2-EU study supports consideration of zamto-cel as a second-line standard treatment option for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma who are ineligible for transplantation.
ab: Background

Anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is the standard second-line treatment for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. However, there is no evidence from randomised controlled trials in patients ineligible for transplantation. To address this gap, we compared zamtocabtagene autoleucel (zamto-cel), a CAR T-cell therapy directed at CD20 and CD19, with rituximab-gemcitabine-oxaliplatin (R-GemOx) chemoimmunotherapy in patients ineligible for transplantation with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma.
Methods

DALY 2-EU is an open-label, multicentre, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted at 45 centres across 12 countries in Europe. Eligible patients were adults (aged ≥18 years) with second-line relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma confirmed histologically who were ineligible for transplantation and had received first-line chemoimmunotherapy containing a combination of an anthracycline-based regimen and an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, with Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status score of 2 or less. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to zamto-cel (single intravenous infusion of 2·5 × 106 fresh (ie, non-cryopreserved) CAR T-cells per kg, capped at 100 kg, produced in a closed automated system) or R-GemOx (rituximab [375 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1], gemcitabine [1000 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2], and oxaliplatin [100 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2] administered for up to eight 14-day cycles). Randomisation was done with an interactive web response system and stratified by age, gender, lactate dehydrogenase, International Prognostic Index, histology, time to relapse after the start of first-line therapy, and country. The primary endpoint was event-free survival assessed by a masked independent review committee and compared all patients randomly assigned to the zamto-cel and R-GemOx groups using a one-sided log-rank test. Safety was assessed in all patients who received study treatment. This ongoing trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04844866).
Findings

Between Oct 14, 2021, and Jul 16, 2024, 219 patients were screened and 160 were randomly assigned to zamto-cel (n=82) and R-GemOx (n=78). The median age was 74·0 years (IQR 70·5-77·0). Patients were predominantly male (100 [63%] of 160 were men and 60 [38%] women) and White (91 [57%]), with race not reported for 64 (40%). Median vein-to-vein time for zamto-cel was 15 days (IQR 15-16). With a median follow-up of 17·0 months (IQR 9·0-22·8), event-free survival was longer in the zamto-cel group than in the R-GemOx group (6·21 months [95% CI 3·84-13·77] vs 2·53 months [1·97-3·35]; HR 0·39 [95% CI 0·27-0·58]; p<0·0001). Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 63 (83%) of 76 with zamto-cel and in 65 (86%) of 76 with R-GemOx. The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were neutropenia (28 [37%] with zamto-cel and 17 [22%] with R-GemOx), anaemia (11 [14%] and 12 [16%]), and decreased neutrophil count (20 [26%] and seven [9%]). Serious adverse events occurred in 31 (41%) patients with zamto-cel and 50 (66%) with R-GemOx, most commonly malignant neoplasm progression (11 [14%] and 38 [50%]), cytokine release syndrome (CRS; six [8%] and none), and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (four [5%] and none). Treatment-related deaths occurred in two (3%) of 82 patients with zamto-cel (due to CRS and haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis) and in one (1%) of 78 with R-GemOx (malignant lymphoma progression).
Interpretation

The risk-benefit ratio observed in the DALY 2-EU study supports consideration of zamto-cel as a second-line standard treatment option for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma who are ineligible for transplantation.

papers.t: Baseline Spleen Volume is Independently Associated With Survival After CD19-Directed Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapy in Relapsed/Refractory Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
papers.c: Baseline spleen volume thus emerges as a readily available imaging-derived marker that could complement established risk factors and refine baseline risk stratification prior to CAR T-cell therapy in r/r DLBCL. Beyond the pretreatment setting, it also has potential utility for prognostication after relapse/progression.
ab: Clinical outcomes after CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy in patients with relapsed or refractory (r/r) diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) remain heterogeneous, underscoring the need for improved risk stratification. As CAR T-cell efficacy is shaped not only by tumor-intrinsic features, host-related factors may also contribute to outcome variability. The spleen, the largest secondary lymphoid organ and a key regulator of immune cell trafficking, is a biologically plausible yet underexplored imaging marker in this setting. We retrospectively analyzed 88 patients with r/r DLBCL and available baseline imaging who received commercial CD19-directed CAR T-cell products between September 2019 and July 2025. Spleen volume was analyzed as a continuous variable (per 100 mL), without dichotomization or prespecified cutoffs, and clinical outcomes were examined in relation to baseline spleen volume. With a median follow-up of 24.4 months, 2-year progression-free survival and overall survival were 40.9% and 56.4%, respectively. Higher baseline spleen volume was associated with inferior overall survival, a higher cumulative incidence of relapse/progression, and inferior post-progression survival. The 24-month risk of death increased progressively with increasing spleen volume. Baseline spleen volume remained independently associated with inferior overall survival after adjustment for established pretreatment risk factors (aHR 1.136 per 100 mL, 95% CI, 1.012-1.275; p = 0.030). Findings were consistent in sensitivity analyses including adjustment for BMI and after exclusion of patients with splenic lymphoma manifestations. Baseline spleen volume thus emerges as a readily available imaging-derived marker that could complement established risk factors and refine baseline risk stratification prior to CAR T-cell therapy in r/r DLBCL. Beyond the pretreatment setting, it also has potential utility for prognostication after relapse/progression.

papers.t: Macular OCTA Biomarkers of Ocular Involvement in Patients With Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma
papers.c: Neither metric showed significant within-group changes over time, and longitudinal analyses revealed no consistent treatment-associated perfusion pattern. These findings identify a predominantly DCP-specific macular microvascular phenotype associated with ocular involvement in PCNSL and support DCP perfusion metrics as candidate noninvasive imaging biomarkers that may complement clinical assessment and intraocular fluid-based evaluation.
ab: Ocular involvement in primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL) can be difficult to identify, highlighting the need for noninvasive biomarkers that may support its detection. We investigated optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) biomarkers associated with ocular involvement in PCNSL. This retrospective single-center study included 62 eyes from 36 patients with PCNSL after exclusion of confounding vitreoretinal disease and poor-quality OCTA scans. Eyes were classified as having ocular involvement (OI; n = 23) or no ocular involvement (NOI; n = 39), and follow-up OCTA was available for 23 eyes from 14 patients. Macular and optic-disc OCTA parameters were analyzed, and discriminatory performance was assessed using direction-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). OI eyes showed predominantly deep capillary plexus (DCP)-specific reductions in macular perfusion. DCP whole-image inferior hemifield perfusion density was lower in OI than NOI eyes (44.95 ± 6.01% vs. 51.06 ± 6.11%; p < 0.001; AUC, 0.776), as was DCP whole-image perfusion density (45.92 ± 6.12% vs. 51.98 ± 6.13%; p < 0.001; AUC, 0.764). In the follow-up subset, the corresponding AUCs were 0.947 and 0.932. Neither metric showed significant within-group changes over time, and longitudinal analyses revealed no consistent treatment-associated perfusion pattern. These findings identify a predominantly DCP-specific macular microvascular phenotype associated with ocular involvement in PCNSL and support DCP perfusion metrics as candidate noninvasive imaging biomarkers that may complement clinical assessment and intraocular fluid-based evaluation.

papers.t: Socioeconomic deprivation does not affect survival outcomes in patients with mantle cell lymphoma: evidence from a German nationwide study
papers.c: This nationwide population-based study indicates that regional socioeconomic deprivation was not associated with clinically relevant differences in survival outcomes among MCL patients in Germany between 2013 and 2023. These findings differ from previously described patterns in other lymphomas, suggesting that biological disease characteristics may exert a stronger influence on MCL survival than social determinants.
ab: Socioeconomic status (SES) is well recognized as an important determinant of cancer incidence and survival. However, its impact on outcomes in patients with mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) remains poorly characterized. We conducted a nationwide, population-based retrospective longitudinal study using German cancer registry data, including all patients diagnosed with MCL between 2013 and 2023. Regional SES was assessed annually at the district level using quintiles of the German Index of Socioeconomic Deprivation. The primary outcomes were 5-year absolute survival (AS) and relative survival (RS) as a proxy for disease-specific survival. A total of 8871 patients were included. Five-year AS and RS were 62.6% (95% CI, 61.5-63.7) and 72.1% (95% CI, 70.8-73.4), respectively. However, no meaningful differences in AS were observed between patients residing in districts of the lowest and highest SES quintiles (62.0% vs 63.1%). This nationwide population-based study indicates that regional socioeconomic deprivation was not associated with clinically relevant differences in survival outcomes among MCL patients in Germany between 2013 and 2023. These findings differ from previously described patterns in other lymphomas, suggesting that biological disease characteristics may exert a stronger influence on MCL survival than social determinants.

papers.t: Immunity and inflammation in classic Hodgkin lymphoma: Bridging diagnosis, prognosis and precision medicine
papers.c: We distinguish diagnostic, prognostic, predictive, and response-monitoring applications and grade biomarkers as established (immunophenotyping, EBER, clinical scores, interim PET), clinically promising (serum TARC, circulating tumor DNA), or investigational (PD-L1-based prediction, spatial and single-cell profiling, artificial intelligence). A deeper understanding of the interplay between immunity and inflammation in cHL may refine disease classification and guide the development of novel immunomodulatory strategies aimed at improving long-term outcomes and overcoming resistance to current therapies.
ab: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) is a unique B-cell malignancy characterized by a small number of malignant Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg (HRS) cells embedded within an extensive and highly organized inflammatory microenvironment. Recent studies have highlighted that the biological behavior of cHL is largely determined by dynamic interactions between HRS cells and surrounding immune populations, including CD4+ T cells, regulatory T cells, macrophages, eosinophils, mast cells, natural killer cells, and stromal elements. HRS cells actively reshape the tumor microenvironment through the secretion of chemokines and cytokines, including CCL17, CCL22, IL-6, IL-10, and TGF-β, promoting immune cell recruitment, chronic inflammation, and immune tolerance. Concurrently, genetic alterations affecting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis, antigen-presentation pathways, and key signaling cascades such as NF-κB and JAK/STAT facilitate immune escape and tumor persistence. We distinguish diagnostic, prognostic, predictive, and response-monitoring applications and grade biomarkers as established (immunophenotyping, EBER, clinical scores, interim PET), clinically promising (serum TARC, circulating tumor DNA), or investigational (PD-L1-based prediction, spatial and single-cell profiling, artificial intelligence). A deeper understanding of the interplay between immunity and inflammation in cHL may refine disease classification and guide the development of novel immunomodulatory strategies aimed at improving long-term outcomes and overcoming resistance to current therapies.

papers.t: Plasma metabolomics and ctDNA analysis in newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: an exploratory study
papers.c: This hypothesis-generating score improved outcome prediction compared with ctDNA assessment alone and enabled the identification of high-risk patients who might benefit from early restaging and potential treatment intensification (24-month PFS 28.8%). In conclusion, plasma metabolomics revealed a prognostically relevant role and 2HB sorted out as a potential host-related biomarker able to refine risk stratification in newly diagnosed DLBCL.
ab: Despite the development of robust prognostic biomarkers for risk stratification in newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), namely international prognostic index (IPI), cell-of-origin (COO), circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and molecular clusters, none of these capture potential host-related features. In this study, untargeted plasma metabolomics was performed in a discovery cohort of 96 newly diagnosed R-CHOP-treated DLBCL patients. The key finding was validated in an independent cohort of 42 DLBCL with comparable clinical characteristics and outcomes. None of the 280 identified plasma metabolites was associated with COO classification subtypes. Conversely, the metabolomic profile appeared to show variations across ctDNA-defined molecular clusters. After an elastic net regression-based survival analysis, 2-hydroxybutyric acid (2HB) was selected as the only endogenous metabolite to be associated with worse progression-free survival (PFS) in the discovery cohort. The impact of 2HB levels on PFS was confirmed in the validation cohort. Also, 2HB levels (HR 2.09, 95% CI 1.04-4.19, p=0.04) maintained an independent association with shorter PFS when adjusted for higher ctDNA levels (HR 2.08, 95% CI 1.06-4.08, p=0.03). Therefore, 2HB and ctDNA levels were included in a two-factor prognostic score based entirely on minimally invasive plasma-derived biomarkers. This hypothesis-generating score improved outcome prediction compared with ctDNA assessment alone and enabled the identification of high-risk patients who might benefit from early restaging and potential treatment intensification (24-month PFS 28.8%). In conclusion, plasma metabolomics revealed a prognostically relevant role and 2HB sorted out as a potential host-related biomarker able to refine risk stratification in newly diagnosed DLBCL.

papers.t: A Rare Case of Hypoglossal Nerve Neurolymphomatosis in a Patient Treated With Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
Nodal T Follicular Helper Cell Lymphoma With Epstein-Barr Virus-Positive Neoplastic T Cells Derived From Clonal Hematopoiesis
papers.c: These findings support a stepwise model of EBV-positive nTFHL arising from TET2-mutated clonal hematopoiesis with subsequent acquisition of a RHOA mutation.
ab: Introduction
Nodal T follicular helper cell lymphoma (nTFHL) with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-positive neoplastic T cells is rare.
Methods
We report a woman with nTFHL and analyzed EBV-infected cells using an immunobead-based method and assessed somatic mutations in lymphoma and lymphoma-uninvolved bone marrow by targeted sequencing.
Results

EBV DNA was enriched in the CD4-positive fraction containing neoplastic T cells. Shared TET2 mutation was identified in both lymphoma and bone marrow, whereas additional TET2 and RHOA G17V mutations were restricted to the lymphoma.
Conclusion
These findings support a stepwise model of EBV-positive nTFHL arising from TET2-mutated clonal hematopoiesis with subsequent acquisition of a RHOA mutation.
Trial Registration
The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

papers.t: Lower baseline eosinophil counts are associated with inferior survival in Mantle cell lymphoma
papers.c: At 3 years, the incident/dynamic AUC increased from 0.674 to 0.707 for OS (p = 0.042) and from 0.653 to 0.680 for PFS (p = 0.057). Higher baseline EOZ was independently associated with favorable outcome in MCL, supporting further evaluation and validation in independent cohorts.
ab: Mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) is characterized by heterogeneous clinical outcomes, highlighting the need for additional biomarkers to refine risk stratification beyond established prognostic models. We evaluated the prognostic value of baseline absolute eosinophil count (EOZ) in 144 adults with newly diagnosed MCL treated with first-line immunochemotherapy. The median EOZ was 0.10 × 109/L. Patients with EOZ above the median had longer OS (84.8 vs. 31.6 months; log-rank p = 0.004) and PFS (64.6 vs. 18.5 months; p = 0.002). In multivariable analyses, each doubling of EOZ was associated with lower hazards of death (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.61-0.87; p < 0.001) and progression or death (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.65-0.89; p < 0.001). At 3 years, the incident/dynamic AUC increased from 0.674 to 0.707 for OS (p = 0.042) and from 0.653 to 0.680 for PFS (p = 0.057). Higher baseline EOZ was independently associated with favorable outcome in MCL, supporting further evaluation and validation in independent cohorts.

The Heterogeneous Landscape of Frontline Treatment of Peripheral T-Cell Lymphomas: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis
papers.c: Our data suggest that BV-CHP may represent a favorable backbone for CD30-positive histologies (ALK-negative ALCL and PTCL-NOS) due to an optimal efficacy-safety balance. Intensive sequential regimens (CEOP/IVE/GDP) provide robust disease control in broad fit populations, while targeted approaches such as Ro-CHOP show promising exploratory signals in AITL/TFH subtypes.
ab: Peripheral T-cell lymphomas (PTCLs) are rare, heterogeneous malignancies with poor prognosis. The optimal frontline strategy remains undefined due to small trial sizes and a lack of direct head-to-head comparisons. A systematic search identified randomized controlled trials evaluating frontline PTCL therapies. Primary Bayesian random-effects and sensitivity frequentist network meta-analyses were conducted to derive HRs, ORs, RRs, and Surface Under the Cumulative Ranking (SUCRA) probabilities across endpoints. Five RCTs comprising 1286 patients across 7 treatment regimens were included: BV-CHP, Ro-CHOP, A-CHOP, GEM-P, the alternating intensified regimen CEOP/IVE/GDP, and standard anthracycline-based backbones (CHOP and CEOP aggregated as the reference arm). In the primary Bayesian random-effects model, sequential CEOP/IVE/GDP demonstrated the highest cumulative likelihood of efficacy across OS, PFS, and ORR, alongside modest tolerability. BV-CHP also demonstrated notable efficacy across response and survival outcomes, paired with the highest safety profile among experimental regimens. In the CD30-unselected LOO sensitivity analysis, CEOP/IVE/GDP maintained leading overall performance, whereas GEM-P and Ro-CHOP formed a closely packed intermediate cluster. Histological subgroup analyses revealed clear therapeutic divergence: BV-CHP showed the highest rank for PTCL-NOS and ALK-negative ALCL, whereas Ro-CHOP showed top ranking for angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma (AITL/TFH). Frontline management of PTCL benefits from histology-driven perspectives. Our data suggest that BV-CHP may represent a favorable backbone for CD30-positive histologies (ALK-negative ALCL and PTCL-NOS) due to an optimal efficacy-safety balance. Intensive sequential regimens (CEOP/IVE/GDP) provide robust disease control in broad fit populations, while targeted approaches such as Ro-CHOP show promising exploratory signals in AITL/TFH subtypes.

Real-world outcomes of glofitamab monotherapy in heavily pretreated patients with relapsed/refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: A multicenter Korean cohort
papers.c: Glofitamab monotherapy demonstrated clinically meaningful activity and manageable safety in heavily pretreated RR-DLBCL. In exploratory analyses, a shorter pre-glofitamab treatment interval was associated with poorer outcomes; this hypothesis-generating observation requires prospective validation.
ab: Glofitamab, a CD20×CD3 bispecific antibody, has shown durable activity in relapsed/refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (RR-DLBCL), but real-world data from Korean patients and after CAR-T failure remain limited. We retrospectively analyzed 46 patients with RR-DLBCL treated with glofitamab monotherapy. Response and safety were assessed in all patients, whereas the main survival and prognostic analyses were conducted in the non-bridge-intent cohort (n = 41), excluding five bridge-intent patients. Median age was 57.5 years; patients had received a median of three prior lines, and 58.7% had failed prior CAR-T. In the overall cohort, the objective response rate was 39.1% and the complete response rate was 32.6%. In the non-bridge-intent cohort, median progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were 2.6 and 5.9 months, respectively, after a median follow-up of 8.2 months. Median duration of response was not reached, and 10 of 15 responders remained in response. Prior CAR-T exposure was not associated with PFS or OS. A longer pre-glofitamab interval was associated with improved PFS (adjusted hazard ratio 0.51 per category increase; p = 0.018), but not OS. Patients with an interval < 1 month had an ORR of 15.4% and median PFS of 1.0 month. Cytokine release syndrome occurred in 26.1%, all Grade 1 or 2; no immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome or treatment-related deaths occurred. Glofitamab monotherapy demonstrated clinically meaningful activity and manageable safety in heavily pretreated RR-DLBCL. In exploratory analyses, a shorter pre-glofitamab treatment interval was associated with poorer outcomes; this hypothesis-generating observation requires prospective validation.

papers.t: BCL6 in B-cell lymphomas: old target, new tricks?
papers.c: In this Perspective, we summarize the roles of BCL6 in B and T cell biology as well as in lymphoma, discuss early efforts at targeting BCL6 and current approaches, and review the results of ongoing early-phase clinical trials of BCL6 degraders. We also explore potential mechanisms of resistance to these agents as well as rational combination therapies.
ab: BCL6 (B Cell Lymphoma 6) is a master regulator of humoral immunity and is required for the germinal center response. Given this role and its frequent dysregulation in germinal center-derived malignancies, it has remained an attractive target since it was first described over 30 years ago. Like other transcription factors, however, it has been difficult to inhibit due to its lack of conventional binding pockets. With the introduction of specific protein degraders, the potential to target BCL6 clinically is now within reach. In this Perspective, we summarize the roles of BCL6 in B and T cell biology as well as in lymphoma, discuss early efforts at targeting BCL6 and current approaches, and review the results of ongoing early-phase clinical trials of BCL6 degraders. We also explore potential mechanisms of resistance to these agents as well as rational combination therapies.

papers.t: A Real-World Experience With First-Line RTOG 0227 (Methotrexate, Temozolomide, and Rituximab) Induction for Primary CNS Lymphoma
papers.c: In this first real-world analysis, MTR induction demonstrated high response rates, durable survival, and excellent tolerability, with comparable outcomes across consolidation approaches, supporting its use as an effective and tolerable first-line therapy for PCNSL.
ab: Background

Primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL) is an aggressive extranodal lymphoma typically treated with CNS-penetrating induction therapy followed by consolidation. Multiple induction and consolidation strategies exist, including whole brain radiation therapy (WBRT), autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT), novel/targeted agents, and conventional chemotherapy. The RTOG-0227 induction regimen (high-dose methotrexate, temozolomide, and rituximab [MTR] followed by WBRT) demonstrated favorable efficacy and tolerability in a phase I/II trial, with no treatment-related mortality. Real-world outcomes for MTR induction remain limited.
Objective
To assess real-world outcomes of patients treated with MTR induction followed by either ASCT or WBRT consolidation.
Study Design

We conducted a single-center retrospective study of adults with newly diagnosed PCNSL treated with MTR induction between 2017 and 2024. Patients subsequently underwent consolidation with ASCT or WBRT. Those who received WBRT continued with temozolomide maintenance. Outcomes included overall response rate (ORR), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS).
Results

Thirty-six patients were included in the analysis (median age 63 years). Following induction, ORR was 89%, with a complete response rate of 25%. Seventeen patients (47%) underwent ASCT and 18 (50%) received WBRT. At a median follow-up of 3.4 years, median OS was not reached, and median PFS was 6.0 years. For patients who responded to MTR induction, 2- and 5-year OS were 97% and 83%, while 2- and 5-year PFS were 83% and 63%, respectively. There were no treatment-related deaths. Survival outcomes did not significantly differ by consolidation strategy.
Conclusions

In this first real-world analysis, MTR induction demonstrated high response rates, durable survival, and excellent tolerability, with comparable outcomes across consolidation approaches, supporting its use as an effective and tolerable first-line therapy for PCNSL.

papers.t: SOHO State of the Art Updates and Next Questions | Best of Cell Therapy for Lymphoma
papers.c: The landscape of cellular immunotherapy in lymphomas has matured from a novel salvage option to a definitive standard of care in earlier lines of therapy for B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. This review consolidates the state of the art clinical data defining the current practice, and examines the next questions driving the field: overcoming antigen escape via dual-targeting constructs (CD19/CD20 or CD19/CD22), the emergence of "armored" CARs to combat the tumor microenvironment, and the promising application of gene-edited allogeneic cells.

papers.t: Omission of Radiation Therapy is Associated with Inferior Disease Control in High Risk Early-Stage Hodgkin Lymphoma
papers.c: Late toxicities were more frequent with CMT, though 69% of second malignancies occurred outside the RT field. These findings support risk-adapted, biomarker-driven treatment selection and the need for prospective trials incorporating modern RT techniques and iPET-adapted algorithms.
ab: Early-stage classical Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is highly curable, yet optimal frontline treatment remains contested. Combined modality therapy (CMT) with chemotherapy followed by radiotherapy (RT) has been the standard, but concern over RT-associated toxicities has driven adoption of chemotherapy-alone approaches despite randomized trials failing to demonstrate noninferiority with RT omission. We analyzed 810 adult patients treated across eight academic centers for stage I/II HL between 1/2012 and 1/2022, comparing outcomes with CMT and chemotherapy alone. Primary endpoints were progression-free (PFS) and overall survival (OS); propensity-score matching was conducted to homogenize baseline characteristics between the groups, and subgroup analyses were conducted to identify clinical features associated with differential benefit. Among 480 propensity-matched patients, five-year OS was 98.6% with CMT versus 97.3% with chemotherapy alone (p=0.620); five-year PFS was 87.2% vs 81.4% (p=0.053). CMT conferred significantly superior PFS in patients with bulky disease (91.8% vs 73.0%; HR 3.77; p=0.005) and interim (iPET)-positive disease (Deauville score (DS)≥4; 74.9% vs 51.9%; HR 2.97; p=0.020). iPET response was the strongest independent predictor of both progression (HR 7.02) and mortality (HR 6.97), with PFS declining markedly across DS groups (DS1-2: 92.2%; DS3: 79.4%; DS4-5: 46.4%). Among iPET-positive patients, those receiving unplanned consolidative RT required less salvage therapy than those managed with chemotherapy escalation alone (29.0% vs. 45.2%; p=0.037). Late toxicities were more frequent with CMT, though 69% of second malignancies occurred outside the RT field. These findings support risk-adapted, biomarker-driven treatment selection and the need for prospective trials incorporating modern RT techniques and iPET-adapted algorithms.

papers.t: CAR T-cell therapy referral patterns and utilization for relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma in the United States
papers.c: Most eligible patients with R/R LBCL did not receive CAR T-cell therapy due to referral gaps or alternative treatment selection at ATCs. Strengthening referral pathways and increasing awareness of the benefits of CAR T-cell therapy may enable broader, more equitable access.
ab: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has improved outcomes for patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) large B‑cell lymphoma (LBCL), yet access in routine clinical practice remains limited. We evaluated referral patterns, durability of clinical benefit, and health care resource utilization (HCRU) among US patients with R/R LBCL. Komodo Health US claims data were retrospectively analyzed (October 2016‒May 2025). Adults with R/R LBCL after ≥2 prior lines of therapy who received CAR T-cell therapy at authorized treatment centers (ATC) were included; patients were stratified by referral and treatment status. Outcomes included referral rates, demographics and subsequent treatment, time‑to‑next treatment or death (TTNT-D), and 12‑month postinfusion HCRU. Among 8959 patients, 20% were referred to an ATC and 15% received CAR T-cell therapy (7% originated at an ATC, 8% referred to an ATC). Referred patients were younger (median age, 61.5 vs 67.3 years; P<0.001) and lived closer to ATCs (median distance 17 vs 24 miles; P<0.001). Among referred patients, baseline demographics were similar between CAR T-cell therapy-treated and nontreated groups. In the second‑line closed‑claims cohort, CAR T-cell therapy recipients had longer TTNT-D compared with the nontreated group (median 28 vs 12 months; P<0.005). Inpatient utilization peaked at 1 month postinfusion (mean 1.54 vs 0.62 visits) before declining to similar rates (0.81 vs 0.59). Most eligible patients with R/R LBCL did not receive CAR T-cell therapy due to referral gaps or alternative treatment selection at ATCs. Strengthening referral pathways and increasing awareness of the benefits of CAR T-cell therapy may enable broader, more equitable access.

papers.t: Care pathway of patients with second-line large B-cell lymphoma treated with CAR T-cell therapies in France
papers.c: Liso-cel was associated with fewer ICU admissions (2.1% vs. 14.1%), less tocilizumab use, a cytokine release syndrome proxy (7.8% vs. 48.3%), and lower three-month rehospitalizations (54.4% vs. 78.1%). ab: CAR T-cell therapies have transformed the management of relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL), with axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel) and lisocabtagene maraleucel (liso-cel) approved after first-line chemoimmunotherapy failure. Real-world data on their care pathway remain limited. This retrospective cohort study used the French national hospital claims database (PMSI) to describe the care pathway and healthcare resource utilization in patients receiving axi-cel or liso-cel as second-line therapy across 32 centers between 2022 and 2024. Among 823 patients (631 [76.7%] axi-cel, 192 [23.3%] liso-cel), bridging was longer with liso-cel (48.5 vs. 38.1 days) and early post-CAR T monitoring shorter (10.9 vs. 16.1 days). Liso-cel was associated with fewer ICU admissions (2.1% vs. 14.1%), less tocilizumab use, a cytokine release syndrome proxy (7.8% vs. 48.3%), and lower three-month rehospitalizations (54.4% vs. 78.1%). These descriptive data show lower hospital resource use with liso-cel than axi-cel as second-line LBCL therapy.

papers.t: Zanubrutinib with rituximab, ifosfamide, carboplatin, and etoposide for relapsed or refractory non-germinal center B-cell lymphoma

ab: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of zanubrutinib plus rituximab, ifosfamide, carboplatin, and etoposide (ZRICE) in patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R), non-germinal center B-cell-like diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Retrospective study of 20 adults (median age 54.4) with R/R DLBCL receiving second-line ZRICE; zanubrutinib 160 mg twice daily for ≤6 cycles. A total of 72 cycles were administered (median 4 per patient). After 2 cycles of ZRICE treatment, the overall response rate (ORR) and the complete response (CR) rates were 90.0% and 70.0%, respectively. The best ORR was 90.0%, and the CR rate was 80.0%. At a median follow-up of 30.5 (range, 5-58) months, the 2-year progression-free survival (PFS) rate was 69.3%, whereas the overall survival (OS) rate was 75.0%, and median PFS and OS were not reached. Common grades ≥4 hematologic adverse events (AEs) included anemia (50.0%) and neutropenia (75.0%). In a real-world setting, ZRICE showed a durable clinical response with tolerable safety in the treatment of R/R DLBCL.

papers.t: Baseline Monoclonal Protein Identifies Plasmacytic Differentiation and Shorter Progression-Free Survival in Marginal Zone Lymphoma
papers.c: In uniformly tested MZL patients requiring systemic therapy, baseline M-protein identifies a subgroup enriched for plasmacytic differentiation and associated with shorter PFS. Post-treatment M-protein decline can support response confirmation when present, but it should not be used as a surrogate endpoint for durable disease control without prospective validation.
ab: Monoclonal protein is frequently tested in marginal zone lymphoma, but interpretation is often inconsistent in practice because prior studies used selective testing and rarely linked serologic findings to biology or post-treatment dynamics. We analyzed 235 adults with newly diagnosed MZL receiving first-line systemic therapy at a single center (2010-2025). All patients had baseline serum protein electrophoresis, immunofixation, and free light chain testing. Plasmacytic differentiation was reviewed by hematopathologists. M-protein response (IMWG criteria) was assessed in patients with post-treatment data. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Baseline M-protein was detected in 117 of 235 patients (49.8%), most commonly immunoglobulin M (IgM) (65.8%). M-protein positivity was associated with a higher frequency of plasmacytic differentiation (39.6% vs. 16.2%; adjusted OR 3.78). M-protein-positive patients had shorter PFS than M-protein-negative patients (median, 50.9 months vs. not reached; log-rank p = 0.044), and this association remained in multivariable analysis (hazard ratio [HR] 1.58). Overall survival (OS), progression of disease within 24 months (POD24), and histologic transformation did not differ significantly by M-protein status. Among 70 patients with evaluable post-treatment data, M-protein response of at least partial response (PR) was highly specific for clinical response and had a high positive predictive value, but response depth did not predict PFS. In uniformly tested MZL patients requiring systemic therapy, baseline M-protein identifies a subgroup enriched for plasmacytic differentiation and associated with shorter PFS. Post-treatment M-protein decline can support response confirmation when present, but it should not be used as a surrogate endpoint for durable disease control without prospective validation.

ab: Hypogammaglobulinemia is increasingly recognized in B-cell malignancies, but whether its clinical significance differs by timing, present at diagnosis versus developing after treatment, remains unclear in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). We retrospectively evaluated 181 adults with newly diagnosed DLBCL treated with rituximab-based immunochemotherapy at a tertiary referral center. Hypogammaglobulinemia was defined as serum IgG < 7 g/L and classified as baseline hypogammaglobulinemia (BHG), treatment-emergent hypogammaglobulinemia (TEHG), or absent. Among the study population, 107 patients (59.1%) developed hypogammaglobulinemia, including 30 (16.6%) with BHG and 77 (42.5%) with TEHG. Patients with BHG exhibited a more adverse baseline clinical profile characterized by poorer performance status and higher-risk disease features. Complete response rates differed significantly across groups and were lowest in patients with BHG (73.3%) compared with TEHG (88.3%) and no hypogammaglobulinemia (94.6%) (p = 0.008). BHG was also associated with the poorest survival outcomes, with median progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) of 26.4 and 30.9 months, respectively. In multivariable analyses, BHG independently predicted infectious complications but was not an independent predictor of PFS. TEHG was associated with shorter PFS in the primary multivariable model; however, this association was not confirmed in a prespecified 6-month landmark analysis. These findings suggest that BHG and TEHG represent distinct clinical states in DLBCL. While BHG identifies a clinically vulnerable subgroup with increased infection risk and inferior outcomes, the prognostic significance of TEHG should be interpreted cautiously because of non-protocolized monitoring and potential ascertainment bias.

ab: Castleman disease (CD) represents a heterogeneous group of hematologic disorders characterized by distinct histopathological features. While CD is regarded as a pre-lymphomatous condition, its reactive or neoplastic nature is still a matter of controversy. Although rare, lymphoma has been reported in patients with CD, most commonly B-cell lymphomas. Here, we present a case of a 69-year-old man initially diagnosed with CD who subsequently developed angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma (AITL) during treatment. To elucidate the potential biological relationship between these two disease entities, we performed whole-exome sequencing to compare genomic alterations between the two disease states. Additionally, we provide a concise review of published cases documenting lymphoma occurring after or coexisting with CD, summarizing patients' characteristics and the various treatment strategies employed thus far.

papers.t: Temporal trends in infectious risk among multiple myeloma patients treated with daratumumab: A meta-analysis
papers.c: Preventive strategies were underused, with <20% of patients with severe respiratory infections receiving immunoglobulin replacement. These findings identify an early window of infectious vulnerability with daratumumab and support temporally targeted prevention and monitoring strategies in contemporary MM care.
ab: Anti-cluster of differentiation 38 (Anti-CD38) monoclonal antibodies such as daratumumab are widely used in multiple myeloma (MM), yet the timing and magnitude of infectious risk remain incompletely defined. We performed an individual patient-level meta-analysis of six randomized trials (N = 2989) comparing daratumumab- versus non-daratumumab-containing regimens in newly diagnosed and relapsed/refractory MM, assessing infectious events over 2 years. Daratumumab-treated patients had higher rates of any-grade (79% vs. 61%) and grade ≥3 infections (29% vs. 20%) than controls, with risk peaking in the first 3 months (42% vs. 36%, p = 0.001) before plateauing. After adjustment, daratumumab was independently associated with grade ≥1 (odds ratio [OR] 1.31, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.10-1.57), respiratory (OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.11-1.71) and grade ≥3 (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.08-2.00) infection by 3 months. Daratumumab-treated patients had a higher rate of infection over 2 years (adjusted incidence rate ratio 1.60, 95% CI 1.47-1.73) and more frequently experienced recurrent infections (33% vs. 22% with multiple any-grade infections; 11% vs. 7% with multiple grade ≥3 infections). Preventive strategies were underused, with <20% of patients with severe respiratory infections receiving immunoglobulin replacement. These findings identify an early window of infectious vulnerability with daratumumab and support temporally targeted prevention and monitoring strategies in contemporary MM care.

ab: The aims of this study were to assess the prognostic value for progression-free survival (PFS) and the diagnostic value (detection rate of multiple myeloma [MM]-related medullary and extra-medullary disease) of whole-body simultaneous [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography coupled with magnetic resonance imaging (WB[18F]FDG-PET/MRI) performed before and after idecabtagene-vicleucel (ide-cel) therapy in patients with triple-class (or more) relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM). A total of 73 patients were prospectively enrolled in this monocentric cohort, and 72 of them underwent WB[18F]FDG-PET/MRI imaging before ide-cel (after personalized bridging therapy). Overall, active disease was detected in 64/72 patients (89%). Multivariate analyses showed that the presence of diffuse bone marrow involvement (BMI) pattern on PET (hazard ratio [HR]: 2.65; 95% CI: 1.16-6.1, P = 0.02) or MRI (HR: 2.69; 95% CI: 1.28-5.66, P = 0.009) was associated with shorter PFS. A total of 66 patients underwent [18F]FDG-PET/MRI for response to ide-cel therapy assessment. Diffusion-weighted MRI (DW-MRI) detected residual disease (response assessment category [RAC]2 or higher according to MY-RADS) in 9/66 patients (14%) and PET (no complete metabolic response according to Deauville score) in 7/66 patients (11%). Overall, [18F]FDG-PET/MRI increased residual disease detection to 13 of 66 patients (20%). Patients with residual disease on DW-MRI (RAC2 or higher) had shorter PFS (HR: 4.11; 95% CI: 1.8-9.4; P < 10-3) than those without (RAC1). Achieving at least a partial metabolic response on PET significantly improved the PFS (P = 0.0046) as well. The combination of [18F]FDG-PET and DW-MRI enabled the identification of three distinct risk groups, including a very high-risk group defined by both MRI and PET positivity.
